theNewYorkTransmissionLetterQuestion.questionPutToThisLane: A previous lane found that the NY court transmission letter ships from TWO families. If VA6's NY family is one of them, say which document it actually delivers and whether the duplication is a defect.
theNewYorkTransmissionLetterQuestion.answer: YES, this lane's NY family is one of the two, and the duplication IS a defect. It is recorded as a ROUTE_IDENTITY failure on the family and carries a repair assignment.
theNewYorkTransmissionLetterQuestion.whichDocumentItActuallyDelivers: Pages 1-2 of the six-page packet are court_transmission_correction_request: a two-page letter titled 'REQUEST TO THE SENTENCING COURT TO TRANSMIT OR CORRECT THE SEALING NOTICE', addressed 'TO: THE RECORDS OFFICE OF THE COURT THAT DISPOSED OF THE CASE NAMED BELOW', asking that office to transmit or correct the CPL Sec. 160.55 sealing notice, enclosing a certificate of disposition. Pages 3-4 are the dcjs_correction_submission letter the family is named for, and pages 5-6 the agency_route_sheet.
whyItIsADefect: The sibling family composed-treatment:obligation:research-decision-route:NY:ny_160_55_violation:sentencing_court_transmission_correction_request is live in MASTER_QUEUE.json at VERIFY_PENDING with its own build script and its own directory, and renders a 4-page packet whose pages 1-2 are the same instrument.

The two letters are neither byte-identical nor textually identical. This family's opens with an express disclaimer, 'THIS IS A LETTER TO A COURT'S RECORDS OFFICE. IT IS NOT A MOTION, A PETITION OR AN APPLICATION, AND IT IS NOT FILED.', and structures the ask as numbered paragraphs 1-4 over five separately labelled certificate-of-disposition blanks. The sibling's structures it as lettered sections A-C with items C1-C4 and no such disclaimer. They are two independent drafts of one instrument.

They do not share a fixture persona. This family localises to '42 Larkspur Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201'. The sibling prints '42 Magnolia Street, Springfield 62704' — a non-New-York placeholder — inside a New York letter.

The route footer is a per-document claim in this factory's own convention: rcap-ok-custom-pleading stamps eight different route footers across its 24 components. All three of this family's components carry the single footer 'Route: obligation:research-decision-route:NY:ny_160_55_violation:dcjs_correction_submission', so the sentencing-court letter wears a route key that is not its own and that a second lane holds a separate grant over.
No record in the repository reconciles the two or says which text governs.
theNewYorkTransmissionLetterQuestion.whatIsNotWrongWithIt: Nothing measured on these six pages is legally or factually wrong. The other fourteen obligations pass, several of them exemplary — both bound committed records verify byte-exact, every fee figure is verbatim from the compiled New York profile, every dotted rule is accounted for in the field map (the only family of the five where that is true), and all six self-help stop conditions are carried. This is a boundary repair, not a rewrite.

contradictionsWithRecordsAlreadyInTheRep.contradiction: MASTER_QUEUE.json records all five families completenessStatus PASS_COMPLETE with allNineCountersZero true, and each family's own reports/completeness-counters.json says allNineZero true. contradictionsWithRecordsAlreadyInTheRep.measured: unclassifiedBlanks: reported 0 / actual 2 for the MS family, 0 / 1 for id_felony_reduction-set, 0 / 16 for rcap-ok-custom-pleading. requiredComponentsMissing: reported 0 / actual 37 for rcap-ok-custom-pleading.
contradictionsWithRecordsAlreadyInTheRep.whyTheCountersMissedIt: For the blanks, the cause is structural and identical in all three build scripts: the blank ledger is constructed only from the field map's refusals — 'for (const r of m.canonicalRefusals ?? []) blanks.push(row(r));' — while the caption dot run is pushed into the component body as a hard-coded literal string rather than through the {{DOTS}} token that registers a field. A literal rule therefore cannot enter the ledger and cannot be counted as unclassified. The literal counts in the scripts match the rendered bytes exactly: 2 for MS against 13 {{DOTS}}, 1 for ID against 8, 16 for OK against 211. I re-ran scripts/rcap-packet-completeness/verify-packet-completeness.mjs myself and it also returned PASS_COMPLETE for all five, because it reads the field map rather than the rendered page.
contradictionsWithRecordsAlreadyInTheRep.consequence: unclassifiedBlanks and requiredComponentsMissing being zero is not evidence of anything on a family built to this shape. This is worth Captain's attention beyond these three families.

Sec. 99-19-72 to petitions under Sec. 99-19-71, and correctly declined to read it across to its own Sec. 99-15-59 route. That is DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 A3 applied exactly right. The seam this lane was told to press hardest is the one that family passes completely.
The ID family carries all four of its registry stop conditions word for word in both artifacts, including the immigration condition with its licensing, peace-officer and firearm limbs intact.

The NY family's fee treatment is the strongest of the five: every figure is the compiled New York profile's own fee-table line verbatim, it discloses the annotation those figures sit under and explains why the charge still reaches this route, and where the profile records an item without an amount it says so and names the office that holds it.

The CT family refused to invent the DESPP submission form its registry classifies as a legal_design_blocker, and said on the packet's face why no submission document exists. Its component set matches its registry contract one to one with no additions — the only family of the five for which that is true.
Zero same-baseline overlapping word pairs across all ten fixtures and 35,975 words, zero off-page ink, and a uniform 72pt left margin on every page of every family.
